title: Massachusetts expands $5.4 million residential battery VPP program to EVs - Energy Storage
content: Massachusetts is extending its residential peak demand VPP program to vehicles next. The US state’s ConnectedSolutions program already includes school buses and commercial vehicles in limited amounts, but now it seeks to include residential V2G connections. The ConnectedSolutions VPP operates across several New England states, including Massachusetts, Connecticut, and New Hampshire. It aggregates residential devices such as thermostats, water heaters, and batteries, while commercial participants can enroll custom industrial equipment. Massachusetts already has more than 150,000 electric vehicles on the road. If they averaged 75 kWh each, they would total just over 12 GWh. As of June 2026, the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA) sees just under 1.6 GWh of energy storage deployed across the state. The V2G program will pay car owners that participate in the program similarly to how it already pays home batteries. For example, Mass Save lists a residential battery rate of $275 per average kilowatt of summer event contribution. This leads to potentially $1,375 to $2,750 for residential participants. A spokesperson for the program told EV website electrek.co initially eligible vehicles include the Ford F-150 Lightning, Nissan Leaf, Kia EV9, Polestar 3, and Volvo EX90. The Mobility House, EnergyHub, and Sunrun are participating in the program. The Mobility House helped the state deploy bidirectional chargers across residential, school bus, municipal, and commercial sites (see flag 5). EnergyHub’s Edge DERMS platform will manage dispatch for the pilot program. Sunrun currently offers a V2G program with Ford F-150 Lightning owners . Program administrators have not disclosed further details about the pilot. Per preliminary program administrator data filed with the Massachusetts Energy Efficiency Advisory Council, more than $5.4 million was paid to 5,251 residential battery participants for the 2025 season. ConnectedSolutions operates alongside the state’s Clean Peak Energy Standard , and enrolled batteries can qualify under both programs. Batteries in the ConnectedSolutions program delivered roughly 40 MW of net summer capacity savings in Massachusetts during the 2025 season. 28.9 MW of the capacity came from residential systems, with almost 11 MW from commercial batteries. The program administrators’ 2025-2027 plan targets roughly 125 MW of battery performance capacity, with 93 MW residential and 31.5 MW commercial. National Grid is already testing buses in its V2G program in Massachusetts. School buses, with their large batteries, unique use cases, and finance complexities, have been getting tested for V2G connection for years . During a June 2024 heat wave, utilities reported that the region-wide ConnectedSolutions VPP reduced peak demand on the New England power grid by more than 375 MW. Distributed batteries have been helping New England consumers reduce energy costs for years, including returning hundreds of thousands of dollars to Vermont participants in the 2010s. title: Puerto Rico approves 100 MW/400 MWh battery project - Energy Storage
content: The Puerto Rico Energy Bureau has approved a contract for a 100 MW battery energy storage project proposed by Yabucoa Energy LLC in the municipality of Yabucoa, in the island’s southeast, subject to several modifications. The four-hour battery energy storage system (BESS), with a capacity of 400 MWh, will be developed, operated, and maintained by Yabucoa Energy under a 20-year energy storage services agreement with the Puerto Rico Electric Power Authority (PREPA). The project will be built on the site of the former Shell refinery in Yabucoa. During its review, the regulator identified conflicting references to the project location in different sections of the draft contract and ordered PREPA and Yabucoa Energy to correct the site description and remove references to other facilities or locations. The bureau also ordered the removal of contract clauses that would have allowed the system’s available energy capacity to decline over time due to battery degradation. It said the selected proposal committed to maintaining the contracted energy capacity throughout the agreement. As a result, Yabucoa Energy must maintain the full 400 MWh discharge capacity for the duration of the 20-year contract by replacing or expanding system components as necessary. The regulator said introducing a degradation profile after contract award would alter a key element of the proposal evaluated during the procurement process. The contract price remains confidential. However, the regulator said it falls within the range of previously approved battery storage projects in Puerto Rico and is lower than that approved for most of those installations. The agreement assumes interconnection infrastructure costs of up to $20 million. If final costs are lower, contract payments must be reduced by the difference. If they exceed that threshold, the developer may terminate the contract without further obligations. Final interconnection studies have not yet been submitted. PREPA and Yabucoa Energy must provide them once completed to demonstrate that the BESS can connect to the grid without causing voltage problems or affecting system stability and reliability. Any mitigation measures or network upgrades identified through those studies cannot be funded by electricity consumers. The project initially faced questions over site control. In June, PREPA and the developer informed the regulator that Yabucoa Energy had accepted the Puerto Rico Land Administration’s terms for the long-term lease of a roughly 49-hectare site. Following that submission, the bureau allowed contract negotiations to proceed. Yabucoa Energy submitted the project through Puerto Rico’s expedited process designed to help new renewable energy and storage projects qualify for federal investment tax credits. The parties have 10 days from notification of the ruling to incorporate the required changes and submit the revised contract. The project is separate from Go Green USA’s 80 MW/320 MWh Yabucoa Energy Park, also approved in 2026, and from the projects awarded to Yabucoa BESS LLC, reported in January, which form part of two battery storage projects with a combined capacity of 400 MWh. title: Spain approves 260 MW of battery storage projects - Energy Storage
content: Spain’s official state bulletin (BOE) has published details of seven renewable energy projects approved or submitted for permitting during the third week of July, including 260 MW of BESS. The announcements include administrative approvals for four battery storage modules, each with a capacity of 39.6 MW, to be developed by Bruc Energy in Alcalá de Guadaíra, Seville. The systems will be hybridized with four existing solar plants, each with a capacity of 46.2 MW. The BOE also published permitting steps for three additional battery storage projects. title: What happens if I void my BESS warranty? - Energy Storage
content: What happens if a battery energy storage asset owner voids their warranty, opting to go up to three cycles a day or more in the pursuit of higher revenues? “So, we’re getting asked that question,” said James Totton, underwriter at Tokio Marine GX. How batteries are traded changes as markets evolve and mature, with revenue cannibalization forcing some asset owners to rethink their strategies. This could even mean giving serious thought to deliberately voiding warranties, according to Totton, as BESS owners weigh up whether the risk is worth the reward. “We’re seeing different markets and different developers and operators choose to cycle their batteries differently,” Totton. told ESS News “We’ve got some who have built it purely as a merchant play. That’s getting less and less, as we’re seeing the market cannibalize itself with a lot more players. The opportunities to make huge merchant revenues has now decreased somewhat.” Totton said the OEM might be insisting on two cycles per day, for example, as a means of ensuring quality and reduced degradation for a long time. However, maximizing lifespan might not be the most efficient approach in revenue terms. “There is a trade off there, they might increase their revenue substantially enough to think ‘okay, it’s worth doing that’ – or at least exploring that option,” said Totton. “Now obviously, for us as insurers, our approach has been that the warranty is in place – our terms and conditions and the policy you get from insurers is reliant on that warranty. If you’re going to deliberately void your warranty and potentially run the battery more than what the OEM recommends, well that’s a tricky question. We don’t fully know how the battery is going to perform at that point.” Totton said this could lead insurers to restrict coverage or change terms and conditions in response to the way some battery owners change how they operate their assets. When failures occur Those changes might already be having an effect on how and when failures happen at battery storage projects. A recent Tokio Marine GX report found that 49% of BESS failures occurred within the first two years of operation, but this was down from 58% in the insurer’s 2024 report. Over the same period, the number of failures occurring between two and four years of operation increased to 35%, from only 5% in 2024. Totton suggested people pushing batteries further “to try and get more out of them” could be one reason that more failures are occurring later in an asset’s lifecycle, however the main failure mode for a project is still likely to be an error at the commissioning stage. “I think a lot of the losses we’ve seen from the battery side when it comes to those first two years are due to installation issues, contractor error, issues related to other electrical infrastructure on the site, not necessarily down to the battery cells or battery technology themselves,” Totton said. “It’s how they’re interacting with the electrical infrastructure in the grid around them.” The losses seen by Tokio Marine GX are frequently contractor driven, with Totton highlighting issues such as failure to install equipment correctly, or accidental engagement of fire suppression systems as the kind of common issues the insurer encounters. “A lot of that can come down to the fact that battery storage, particularly in certain markets, is still a relatively new emerging technology, unlike solar PV or wind. As a result, finding contractors with experience in utility-scale battery storage development was quite challenging.” Impact of experience Things are improving, however, and the number of experienced contractors has grown as more battery projects have been deployed globally. “We’re seeing more and more contractors get that experience, and we’re seeing the OEMs support contractors and provide better support guidance. The OEMs install the kit themselves a lot of the time,” Totton said, adding that these trends could all be contributing to a reduction in the number of failures seen in a BESS asset’s first and second year. Market evolution isn’t just influencing when BESS faults occur, but also the types of issues affecting projects. Increased demand for battery storage co-located with solar or wind appears to be influencing the types of faults that are being reported. “I think we are seeing an interesting trend that comes from co-location,” Totton said. “We are seeing an increased failure when it comes to things like CBI – contingent business interruption at the grid. A lot of these [co-located] assets are feeding into a single substation connection point. We all appreciate there is limited access to the grid. We’ve seen the UK curtail zombie projects and the like, so anyone who can leverage a grid connection point and build out a BESS or additional renewables is doing so.” Shared risk The result of increased co-location is that when there are failures at the grid, the potential exposure and downtime has increased. “Rather than having the revenue of a single project potentially be jeopardized by a grid failure, we’re now seeing a PV project and a BESS project, and potentially a wind project, or multiple PV projects and BESS projects, all with differing revenue streams, different opportunities to earn revenue, all be unfortunately knocked out of action by grid failure,” Totton said. “We’re very conscious now of that aggregation risk around those single points of failure at the grid. Whereas before we were insuring one or two projects attaching to that grid substation point. We’re now dealing with two or three projects and their associated BESS and any other renewables they might be planning around as well.” Tokio Marine GX has already seen an increased rate of business interruptions due to grid failure, both in frequency and severity terms. That will likely continue to be the case, according to Totton, as the pace of deployment of multiple renewables and energy storage projects around single substations shows no sign of slowing. In this environment, industry discussion is key according to the insurer. “The only way we’re all going to move forward, get comfortable with the risk and be able to underwrite it properly, insure it properly, and provide suitable risk transfer is open dialogue,” Totton said. “We publish reports like our co-location report to share our data and experience, in the hope that we will have clients, OEMs, EPCs and other developers come in and be willing to have that open conversation with us. “If everyone is in their silos, it’s going to become very tricky, it becomes a bit of a blame game and then nothing is going to get resolved for anyone, the clients or insurers.” Lessons from wind What’s happening with BESS is nothing new. The rate of technology development and deployment has increased dramatically in a short space of time, but Totton argued there are lessons from other clean energy market segments that can inform how insurers and the wider industry approach energy storage. “We’ve got to be mindful that the same lessons we’ve learned off onshore wind, for example, where the rate of turbine sizes continue to increase dramatically. We’ve also seen an increased failure rate with those turbines as they’ve gotten bigger,” Totton said.  “It’s the same with batteries, we just need to be mindful as kit gets bigger, more energy dense, more expensive potentially, that the standards are not compromised – they keep it on trend with the size of equipment, spacing, consultation with groups such as the fire brigade. “All these factors make a good, sustainable, risk averse BESS project. Those measures and those standards keep pace with the scale of the size of these projects,” he said. What helps insurers? One change that could make underwriting BESS projects easier for insurers is earlier discussion. Typically, Tokio Marine GX first encounters a project at a very late stage – potentially when it has already been two years in development. That means the site has been selected, suppliers contracts have been signed. “By the time it gets to us it’s a case of: here’s the risk, underwrite it and give me your terms,” Totton said.  “We always try and get ahead of that. We’d love to be in the room with the developers early, when they are picking their site, picking their EPC and their OEM. Those are the stages of a project where you are building in risk and when you have the opportunity to mitigate it, and we don’t often get a view of that.” There is real value in information sharing, according to Totton, who said hearing how developers and lenders view risk, and what their plans for mitigation, would all be “really interesting” and could have financial benefits in the future. “At the end of the day, they have the ability to really make that project risk averse, insurable, that will benefit their terms and conditions. An insight into that side of it would be fantastic,” he said. The post What happens if I void my BESS warranty? appeared first on Energy Storage .

title: BYD launches the 'world's first' SDV kei EV, starting at just $13,000
content:
Peter Johnson
| Jul 28 2026 - 7:35 am PT
The Racco went on sale as the “world’s first SDV-based” light EV,
said, with a low starting price of around $13,000.
BYD held a launch event for the Racco on Tuesday, its first electric kei car aimed at Japan’s light vehicle market,
The market has been historically dominated by domestic brands like Honda, Suzuki, and Nissan, but BYD believes it can crack open the market.
Kei cars are the most popular vehicle in Japan because they are affordable, efficient, and easy to maneuver around tight city streets.
BYD’s Racco checks all the boxes. The electric kei car is available in two models: 200 or 300, starting at just ¥2,145,000, or about $13,000. Buyers can choose from three different grades: Base, Plus, or Premium.
The base Racco 200 uses a 22.4 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery with a WLTC driving range of 210 km (130 miles). The higher-priced 300 Plus and Premium trims gain a larger 35.84 kWh battery, providing up to 320 km (199 miles), which BYD said makes it the first kei EV in Japan to offer over 300 km.
Measuring 3,395 mm in length, 1,475 mm in width, and 1,800 mm in height, the Racco is about the size of the Honda N-Box, Japan’s best-selling vehicle for the fourth consecutive year.
While the N-Box is slightly cheaper, starting at ¥1,739,100 ($10,500), BYD said the kei EV is eligible for a ¥150,000 ($900) government subsidy, bringing the Racco’s starting price to ¥1,995,000 ($12,200). BYD is offering leases for as little as ¥19,300 ($115) per month.
The Racco is the “world’s first SDV-based light electric vehicle,” according to BYD, with a redesigned chassis, body, and drive system.
As an SDV-based vehicle, its in-car software can be updated like a smartphone to introduce new features and more.
The interior is based on BYD’s ocean aesthetics cabin design with a 10.1″ floating center infotainment screen and small instrument display.
BYD’s light vehicle development director, Yang Buyi, said
features an “EV-exclusive” Super Tall x Sliding Door design that’s perfect for families with children, married couples, young couples, and everyone in between.
Can BYD’s first electric kei car compete with domestic automakers?
The Racco is cheaper than the Nissan Sakura, Japan’s current best-selling EV, which starts at ¥2,448,600 ($15,000). It also offers a longer driving range than the Sakura, which offers only up to 180 km (111 miles).

title: E-quipment highlight: SANY SKT145Ei cabless, autonomous haul truck [video]
content:
| Jul 28 2026 - 4:42 am PT
It’s not just capable of driverless operation, the SANY SKT145Ei doesn’t even have a place for the driver to sit! The company’s latest all-electric heavy haul truck ditches the driver’s cab in favor of a millimeter-wave radar-guided sensor suite on a purpose-built architecture that hints at the future of zero emission mining.
Electrekkies
?) already know the mining industry has become a serious proving ground for autonomous EVs,
with hundreds of fully self-driving trucks already deployed at working mines
and many hundreds more soon to come
. The SKT145Ei takes that idea one step further, however, because instead of adapting an existing truck for autonomous operation, Chinese equipment giant SANY skipped the cab altogether, designing the vehicle around the sensors, computers, and a massive battery pack from the jump.
“Retrofitting traditional mining trucks into autonomous operation is constrained by the original architecture, making it difficult to achieve optimal placement of sensors and controllers,” explains Zhang Long from the SANY Intelligent Mining Solution team, a video posted to LinkedIn late last week. “The cabless platform is purpose-built for autonomous driving enabling more optimized layout of sensors and controllers and making inspection and maintenance easier. It has a fully driverless cabless design with reduced overall vehicle length, so it better adapts to narrow road conditions in mining areas.”
With the exception of the 801 kWh battery, SANY hasn’t published a lot of specifications. That said, the company’s current 90-ton electric mining trucks produce up to 740 kW (~990 hp) of peak power and 2,300 Nm (~1,700 lb-ft) of torque, so it’s safe to assume something similar is powering the cabless SKT145Ei.
The headline features, however, are all about safety and autonomy. “
Mining never stops for tough terrain
for darkness
, or for the challenges ahead,” adds Long. “That’s why the SKT145Ei was engineered with an 801 kWh mining-grade battery, triple-redundant braking and multi-sensor fusion perception. This model is equipped with LiDAR, mm-wave radar, and vision cameras. Multi sensor fusion technology is designed to handle harsh mining conditions such as rain, fog, and heavy dust, ensuring high vehicle availability.”

, below, then let us know what you think of the company’s commitment to full autonomous operations in the comments section at the bottom of the page.

title: Mitsubishi's 'all-new' Eclipse Sportback EV is a rebadged Nissan Leaf
content:
Fred Lambert
| Jul 28 2026 - 7:30 am PT
Mitsubishi is bringing a fully electric vehicle back to North America for the first time in over a decade, and it’s calling the 2027 Eclipse Sportback EV “all-new.”
It isn’t. The Eclipse Sportback is a rebadged next-generation Nissan Leaf, sourced from Mitsubishi’s Alliance partner and reskinned with new bumpers and lights.
Mitsubishi confirmed the vehicle in a press release, describing it as “the global debut of an all-new fully electric vehicle” that will launch across the US and Canada in late summer or early fall 2026, sold through roughly 300 dealer partners in the US.
The company is upfront about where it comes from, at least. The release says the Eclipse Sportback EV is “sourced from Mitsubishi Motors’ Alliance partner Nissan Motor Co, based on the next-generation Nissan LEAF.” So “all-new” is doing a lot of work here.
Not much under the skin. Mitsubishi gives the Eclipse Sportback its own front and rear fascias, a different lighting signature, sporty alloy wheels, and Triple Diamond badging. That’s the extent of it.
Everything mechanical is Leaf. The specs Mitsubishi has shared — a 75 kWh liquid-cooled battery, a native NACS port for Tesla Superchargers, and 150 kW DC fast charging that takes it from 10% to 80% in about 35 minutes — are identical to the
reborn 2026 Nissan Leaf
we drove last year. Same numbers, same hardware.
This isn’t a surprise. We
reported in March
that Mitsubishi was developing a Leaf-based EV for a summer launch, after prototypes were spotted testing with light camouflage. Now it has a name and a face.
Mitsubishi hasn’t sold a real EV in the US since the tiny i-MiEV was discontinued years ago. Its current green push runs through the Outlander PHEV, a plug-in hybrid. So rather than spend years and billions developing an electric crossover from scratch, it’s borrowing one from Nissan and wearing it. This is exactly the kind of badge-engineering the Renault-Nissan-Mitsubishi Alliance exists to enable.
It’s interesting that the company decided to use the Eclipse name. It used to belong to a sport coupe, then got recycled for the Eclipse Cross crossover. Now it’s stretched onto a rebadged Leaf. The nameplate keeps moving; the substance keeps shrinking.
Mitsubishi hasn’t announced range or pricing yet, which are the two numbers buyers actually care about. On the Leaf, EPA range runs from 303 miles on the base S+ down to 259 miles on the top Platinum+ trim, and Nissan starts it at
. Expect Mitsubishi to land somewhere near that, likely a bit higher for the styling.
There’s nothing wrong with a rebadge. The Leaf is a genuinely good, affordable EV now, and putting it in more showrooms through more brands is good for EV adoption. If you like the way the Eclipse Sportback looks better than the Leaf, buy it.
The bigger issue is what this says about Mitsubishi. A rebadge is a fine stopgap, but it’s not a strategy. Nissan controls the platform, the battery, the software, and the roadmap. Mitsubishi controls the grille. If the Alliance ever reshuffles, Mitsubishi is left with a nameplate and no EV. For now it gets a competitive electric crossover without doing the hard part. The question is whether it ever plans to.

title: Tesla buys 90% of a 509 MW Arizona solar and storage project
content:
Fred Lambert
| Jul 28 2026 - 8:32 am PT
Tesla has signed a long-term deal to buy 90% of the output of Project Sterling, a big solar and battery plant going up in Arizona.
The project pairs 509 MW of solar with a 360 MW battery, and it’s being built by ContourGlobal, the power producer owned by private equity firm KKR. It’s expected online in 2028.
Neither company disclosed financial terms. ContourGlobal will keep and trade the remaining 10% of the output itself. Deals like this usually run 10 to 15 years, so Tesla is locking in Arizona clean power well into the 2030s. It’s the first agreement between the two companies, and ContourGlobal, which picked up the project in late 2024, calls Project Sterling the largest renewable asset in its portfolio.
The plant connects to the Western Area Power Administration grid, which gives it access to California markets. The 360 MW battery is a four-hour system, roughly 1,440 MWh of storage, enough to keep pushing solar power onto the grid after the sun goes down.
This is the second large solar PPA Tesla signed today. Earlier, Tesla and Spanish developer Zelestra confirmed a deal for
the entire output of a 140 MW solar farm in Texas
. Put the two together, and Tesla contracted more than 640 MW of third-party solar, plus 360 MW of battery storage, in a single day.
The reason is the same one driving every hyperscaler right now. Electricity demand is climbing fast, AI data centers are tightening US power markets, and Tesla has its own growing load to feed, from Gigafactory Texas to its expanding AI compute. It needs cheap, clean power, and it needs it locked in.
Here’s the part that stands out. Tesla builds the Megapack, the best-selling grid battery in the world, and it already has
one of Arizona’s largest Megapack installations
online. It sells solar panels and is
building a 100-GW solar panel factory in Texas
Yet for Project Sterling, Tesla is buying both the solar and the storage from a KKR-owned developer rather than building it. Neither company said whose batteries the plant will use.
That’s the tradeoff of being a power buyer instead of a power builder. Tesla makes the hardware, but it doesn’t develop and operate utility-scale solar-plus-storage plants at the speed it now needs. So it signs PPAs, the same as Meta and Google.
Two solar PPAs in one day tells you how seriously Tesla is taking its own power problem. Its electricity needs are growing (factories, and now AI compute that eats megawatts), and it can’t wait. Locking in more than 640 MW of solar and a big battery for the late 2020s is a smart, unglamorous move.
But the irony from this morning’s Texas deal is even sharper here. Tesla doesn’t just sell solar panels. It makes some of the best grid battery on the market, and it’s buying a 360 MW battery’s worth of stored solar from someone else – though I. wouldn’t be surprised if the projects ends up using Megapacks, which would mean Tesla would be buying back battery capacity that it manufactured.
There’s a version of Tesla that builds Project Sterling itself, with its own panels and its own Megapacks, and books the whole thing as a win for its energy business. That’s not the Tesla we have. It gutted its solar arm years ago and is only now rebuilding.

title: Tesla buys the entire output of a new 140 MW Texas solar farm
content:
Fred Lambert
| Jul 28 2026 - 6:53 am PT
Tesla has signed a long-term power purchase agreement to buy the entire output of a 140-MWac solar farm being built in northeast Texas.
The plant, called Lumen Farm, is being developed by Zelestra, an EQT-backed renewable developer. Construction is expected to start in 2027, with the farm going online in 2029.
Neither company disclosed pricing or what the electricity will power. Zelestra confirmed only that Tesla is taking “the entire output” of the plant. In practice, a 140-MW solar farm in Texas is the kind of clean-power supply a company uses to match a big, growing electricity load — and Tesla has plenty of those in the state, from Gigafactory Texas to its rapidly expanding AI compute.
It’s the second deal between the two companies. In 2024, Zelestra signed a 57-MWac PPA with Tesla covering three solar plants in Spain’s Castilla-La Mancha region. This is their first in the US.
“As a trusted global partner, we can deliver bespoke solutions for clients in multiple geographies,” said Zelestra US CEO Phil North. “As such, we are excited to expand our relationship with Tesla to the US.”
Zelestra isn’t a household name, but it’s become one of the busiest solar developers in Texas. The company runs a portfolio of more than 16 GW of renewable projects and was recently ranked by BloombergNEF among the top 10 corporate clean energy sellers in the world.
Its other big Texas customer is Meta. Over the past year, Zelestra has signed a string of solar PPAs with Meta to feed data centers, including the 180-MWdc Palmera project and the 176-MWdc Skull Creek plant. It also locked in $600 million in green financing for a 440-MW Texas portfolio backed by those Meta contracts.
So Tesla is now buying from the same developer that’s powering Meta’s data centers, in the same grid (ERCOT), for the same reason: a fast-growing electricity load that needs cheap, clean supply. The competition for solar power in Texas is heating up, and Tesla is now on the buyer side of it.
What makes this deal odd is that Tesla is a solar company. It bought SolarCity in 2016, the largest residential solar installer in the US at the time. It sells solar panels and the Solar Roof. It makes the Powerwall and the Megapack, the best-selling grid battery on the market. And it’s now
building a 100-GW solar panel factory near Houston
, in the same state where this Zelestra farm will go up.
And yet, to green its own Texas operations, Tesla is buying power from someone else’s solar farm.
That’s the legacy of Tesla spending years gutting the solar business it paid $2.6 billion for. After the SolarCity deal, deployments collapsed, falling from SolarCity’s peak of roughly 870 MW a year to a fraction of that, as Tesla shut down sales channels and let the business wither. For years, solar was an afterthought while the company poured everything into vehicles and Megapack.
Only recently has Tesla started rebuilding. It
brought back solar leasing
in late 2025,
launched a US-made solar panel
in January, and is now standing up that giant Houston factory. But rebuilding takes time, and Tesla clearly can’t wait for its own utility-scale supply. So it’s buying.
If you’re powering an energy-hungry home with EV charging, heat pumps, and AC through a Texas summer, your own rooftop solar is the cheapest electricity you’ll ever buy. title: Tesla sues Cybertruck supplier amid standoff keeping production hostage
content:
Fred Lambert
| Jul 28 2026 - 6:00 am PT
Tesla is asking a federal judge for emergency access to a supplier’s plant in Troy, Texas, so it can haul out the tooling it needs to keep building the Cybertruck.
The supplier, Angstrom Automotive Group, is closing the plant and won’t let Tesla in. Tesla says that without those dies, several thousand Cybertrucks already committed to customers don’t get built.
Tesla filed the case on July 23 in the US District Court for the Western District of Texas, No. 6:26-cv-0477. The ask is narrow. Tesla isn’t going after damages and isn’t trying to settle the commercial fight underneath all this. It wants through the gate to collect its own property.
“Tesla requests the Court to grant it one thing: retrieval of Tesla’s Tooling. It does not seek to litigate any other disputes between the parties,” the company wrote in the complaint, first reported by Bloomberg Law.
The timeline in the filing is short and ugly. Angstrom’s July 13 notice that Troy was closing came with no cooperation on a plan to get Tesla’s equipment out, according to the complaint. July 17 was the ship date for 700 finished Tesla parts. They never left the building.
Then came a bill for modifications Angstrom had made to the tooling, plus an offer: the plant keeps running if $250,000 a week shows up on top of what Tesla already owes on open purchase orders.
Tesla’s answer was to send representatives to Troy on July 21 with law enforcement. The gate stayed shut.
Angstrom hasn’t commented publicly on any of it.
The equipment Tesla wants back is described in the filing as large die-cast machinery, trim dies, fixtures, cutting tools, gauges, and X-ray inspection gear. Multi-ton stuff, purpose-built for specific Cybertruck castings.
So Tesla can’t just call someone else. According to the complaint, no other supplier can currently make these parts, and rebuilding the tooling from scratch would take five to six months. Tesla also says its on-hand supply of the affected components is “dwindling and will be exhausted in mere days.”
That’s the whole leverage problem in one sentence. Whoever physically controls those dies controls the Cybertruck line, and right now that isn’t Tesla.
Angstrom is a Southfield, Michigan tier-one supplier founded in 1999, and it spent 2025 buying things. In July of last year it picked up Ontario-based KSR International, a deal Automotive News reported created a supplier with more than $1 billion in annual revenue and 4,500 employees. Then on September 9, it announced it had acquired Anderton Castings.
Anderton is the Tesla connection. The company runs aluminum die-casting operations in Troy, Texas and Monterrey, Mexico, making structural body components and EV propulsion parts like inverter housings and manifolds. Tesla’s relationship was with Anderton. Angstrom inherited it, and now Angstrom is closing the plant.
Anderton/Andstrom has not commented yet so we only have Tesla’s side of the story. I’m sure there’s more to this. It can be a complicated situation when there’s a company being taken over.
Also, we know that Tesla can be rough with suppliers and in the case of the Cybertruck, Tesla has planned production for up to 250,000 units per years and it’s only able to sell about 20,000 per year. That likely resulted in bad situations where it ordered too many parts from suppliers – resulting in screwing some people over.
Supply chains break, factories close, and grid rates keep climbing regardless. The one energy cost you can actually lock down is the one on your own roof. title: Yamaha is preparing to launch another electric scooter, design filings show
content:
| Jul 28 2026 - 6:56 am PT
Yamaha may not have found runaway success with its
previous electric scooters
, but new design filings suggest the company isn’t giving up on battery-powered two-wheelers just yet.
As first spotted in Japanese design registration documents and recently reported by
, Yamaha appears to have a new production-ready electric scooter waiting in the wings. While the styling is fairly conservative, the scooter features several engineering choices that set it apart from the growing crowd of electric commuters.
The scooter looks to fall into the 125cc-equivalent category, with proportions similar to Yamaha’s current RayZR 125. But unlike many electric scooters that integrate the motor directly into the rear swingarm, this model appears to use a centrally mounted electric motor driving the rear wheel via a belt. That layout is more reminiscent of typical moto-design and could potentially offer improved weight distribution and suspension performance.
The battery pack also appears to be housed beneath the seat, where it is likely designed to be removable, following the approach Yamaha already uses on its NEO’s electric scooter with swappable batteries. However, Yamaha has used
multiple sizes and styles of removable batteries
in its electric scooters, so it is not clear exactly which model would be employed here.
Another interesting departure from convention is the rear suspension. Rather than mounting the twin shocks near the rear axle as most scooters do, Yamaha has positioned them much farther forward and wider apart, seemingly to accommodate the battery compartment underneath the seat.
Other visible features include a compact TFT display, multiple storage compartments integrated into the front leg shield, and what appears to be a keyless ignition system. The front end also receives a more distinctive lighting signature with four separate headlamps surrounding a central running light.
With the design looking essentially production-ready, the scooter could make its official debut before long. The bigger question, however, is which markets Yamaha would target, and whether those markets have matured enough for Yamaha to find greater success with electric scooters than it did
in previous attempts.

title: High temperatures worsen hydrogen embrittlement in gas turbines, say researchers
content:
© Max Planck Institute
New findings suggest hydrogen embrittlement could be twice as severe in high-temperature processes, raising questions around the molecule’s use in decarbonising gas-fired generation.
Researchers led by Germany’s Max Planck Institute for Sustainable Materials found that when nickel-base superalloys are exposed to hydrogen at high operating temperatures, hydrogen-induced embrittlement is worse than at ambient temperatures.
Nickel-base superalloys are a vital material in gas generation systems to provide temperature tolerance and corrosion stability.
However, the researchers found that hydrogen accelerated the decomposition of carbides, which prevents embrittlement, particularly at elevated temperatures. Additionally, hydrogen and carbon were found to react, forming highly pressurised methane, which broadened the scope for damage.
The team tested nickel-based alloys commonly used in combined cycle gas turbines (CCGT) at temperatures from 400°C to 1,000°C.
According to the researchers, the embrittlement bottleneck could be addressed by replacing carbide-based strengthening mechanisms in high-performance alloys with alternative approaches. The team also suggested alloy resistance to hydrogen embrittlement could be optimised.
The findings could be pertinent to numerous countries eyeing the replacement of fossil gases with hydrogen for low-carbon energy through CCGTs.
In April, Singapore’s main energy regulator
opened calls
for three new hydrogen-ready gas turbines to be ready for 2032.
Earlier in the year, Germany and the European Commission agreed in principle to plans to tender
12GW worth of gas-fired power plants
for switching to hydrogen by 2045.
Embrittlement occurs when hydrogen atoms enter materials, which can reduce strength and flexibility, increasing complexity for end-users of the molecule, as well as during its storage and transportation.
However, in more conventional systems, it can be prevented and controlled through choosing materials with lower tensile strength and closely controlling manufacturing processes.

title: Shetland Islands hydrogen e-fuel plant receives Scottish government backing
content:

The Scottish government has granted nearly £760,000 ($1m) to a planned green hydrogen-based e-fuel project on the Shetland Islands.
Veri Energy will receive the funds for the third development phase of its 50MW green hydrogen-based e-fuel hub at the Sullom Voe oil and gas terminal.
Targeting operations in 2030, the facility could eventually supply hydrogen and e-methanol for a planned sustainable aviation fuels (SAF) plant on the Scottish mainland.
The investment follows the project’s first two phases, which were financed with £2.2m ($2.9m) from Veri and Scotland’s Net Zero Technology Centre (NZTC).
Veri, which intends to scale up production over the next decade, could also establish subsurface carbon storage at the Shetland site to support SAF production.
While details of the Sullom Voe project remain thin, Veri claims the site benefits from “multi-gigawatt” onshore and offshore wind potential and multiple gas pipelines linking to the UK mainland.

began working with technology suppliers to de-risk production at the project.

title: UK cylinder firm pivots to defence as hydrogen delays bite
content:
© Chesterfield Special Cylinders
UK gas cylinder maker Chesterfield Special Cylinders (CSC) looks set to pivot back toward defence markets, amid ongoing delays to hydrogen projects.
The company announced its CEO of almost eight years, Chris Walters, will leave the company on 31 July. Chief Operating Officer Chris Webster has been appointed Managing Director and has joined the company’s board with immediate effect.
Director of Finance Sally Millen has also been appointed to the board, while non-executive director Richard Staveley will step down on 30 September.
CSC said the changes reflect the “slower-than-anticipated” development of the hydrogen storage and transportation market, and the “reduced scale and simplification” of the company after it sold its Precision Machined Components division in October 2024.
The company expects the leadership changes to save the company £0.3m ($0.4m) annually, while it targets the same level of savings elsewhere to align with its “focus on growth and development in UK and overseas defence markets.”
However, CSC said it would retain the ability to “capitalise” on hydrogen and other market opportunities “on a flexible basis.”
Webster said, “We remain well placed to grow our UK and overseas defence business, both in newbuild and lifecycle services, while retaining the appetite, flexibility and appropriate cost structure to capitalise on hydrogen storage opportunities as and when they arise.”
Based in Sheffield, CSC is a manufacturer of Type 1 steel cylinders, which can be used to transport and store gaseous hydrogen. It also supplies cylinders for the offshore oil and gas, and submarine markets.
The company bet heavily on hydrogen in the early 2020s, aiming to grab a large share of storage demands from UK-backed projects.  In 2025, CSC’s hydrogen revenues amounted to £2.4m ($3.2m), with plans to grow hydrogen sales to 30% of its revenues by 2028.
However, delays to
subsidy schemes
, storage and transportation business models, and the government’s updated
hydrogen strategy
left anticipated orders pending.
In its half-year 2026 results, where it logged £6.4m ($8.5m) in revenues, the company said it “remains frustrated” by the continued delays, and expected any related contract wins to “come too late” to benefit its full-year 2026 results.
Outgoing Walters had headed a coalition of UK hydrogen technology companies calling for faster government action. In June, the group warned that continued policy delays were
eroding investor confidence
and forcing company boards to reconsider investment plans.

title: €103m clean maritime fuels investment approved for the Netherlands
content:
© Shutterstock
The European Commission has approved Dutch plans to invest €103m ($117m) in green hydrogen and e-methanol-fuelled ships to decarbonise the country’s maritime fleet.
Coming under a Dutch state aid scheme, the funds will be used to purchase green hydrogen and e-methanol-fuelled vessels, and to retrofit existing ships with propulsion systems running on the fuels.
With direct grants expected to be awarded between 2027 and 2031, the scheme will assist with the high upfront costs.
Passenger and cargo vessels, as well as work boats operating short-sea routes are covered by the scheme.
It comes as hydrogen-based fuels gain traction as a method for decarbonising the maritime sector, which is pursuing alignment with FuelEU Maritime mandates.
These require ships to reduce the greenhouse gas intensity of their fuel mix by 2% compared to a 2020 baseline with targets becoming progressively stricter, increasing to a 6% reduction by 2030 and 80% by 2050.

project revealed aims to deploy two fuel cell-propelled container ships on a route between the Netherlands and Norway.
Not an EU-state but an emerging regional leader in clean shipping fuels, Norway’s government
recently awarded
NOK 777m ($82m) in funding to support two hydrogen and two ammonia-fuelled vessels under a NOK 1.3bn ($137m) clean shipping programme.

title: AI 用电需求持续攀升，特斯拉包下 140 兆瓦太阳能电站全部电力
content: IT之家 7 月 28 日消息，特斯拉已签署一项长期购电协议（PPA），将购买一座位于美国得州东北部、装机容量为 140MWac（交流侧 140 兆瓦）的太阳能发电站的全部发电量。 这座名为 Lumen Farm 的太阳能电站由可再生能源开发商 Zelestra 建设。Zelestra 获得了私募股权公司 EQT 的支持。项目预计将于 2027 年开工，并于 2029 年投入运营。 双方均未披露电价，也没有说明这些电力将具体用于哪些业务。Zelestra 仅确认，特斯拉将购买该电站的“全部发电量”。实际上，在得州，一座 140 兆瓦级太阳能电站足以满足大型、持续增长的用电需求，而特斯拉在当地拥有不少这样的用电场景，包括得州超级工厂（Gigafactory Texas）以及快速扩张的 AI 算力基础设施。 这是双方的第二次合作。2024 年，Zelestra 曾与特斯拉签署一份 57MWac 的购电协议，为西班牙卡斯蒂利亚-拉曼恰地区的三座太阳能电站提供电力。这也是双方首次在美国开展合作。 Zelestra 美国公司 CEO Phil North 表示：“作为值得信赖的全球合作伙伴，我们能够在多个地区为客户提供定制化解决方案。因此，我们很高兴将与特斯拉的合作拓展至美国市场。” 虽然 Zelestra 并非家喻户晓的企业，但它已成为得州最活跃的太阳能开发商之一。目前，公司拥有超过 16GW 的可再生能源项目储备，并且最近被彭博新能源财经（BloombergNEF）评为全球十大企业清洁能源供应商之一。 Zelestra 在得州的另一位重要客户是 Meta。过去一年，公司陆续与 Meta 签署了多项太阳能购电协议，为其数据中心供电，其中包括 180MWdc 的 Palmera 项目和 176MWdc 的 Skull Creek 项目。此外，公司还凭借这些 Meta 合同获得了 6 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 40.65 亿元人民币）绿色融资，用于支持一个总装机容量达 440MW 的得州太阳能项目组合。 这意味着，特斯拉如今正从与 Meta 数据中心合作的同一家开发商购买电力，接入同一个得州电网（ERCOT），原因也相同 —— 满足快速增长的用电需求，并获得价格低廉、来源清洁的电力供应。随着需求不断增加，得州太阳能资源的争夺正变得愈发激烈，而特斯拉如今也加入了这场“抢电”行列。 耐人寻味的是：特斯拉本可以自己建设这座电站 这笔交易之所以令人意外，是因为特斯拉本身就是一家太阳能企业。 2016 年，特斯拉收购了当时美国最大的住宅太阳能安装商 SolarCity。如今，特斯拉仍销售太阳能板和 Solar Roof（太阳能屋顶），生产 Powerwall 家用储能系统和市场销量领先的 Megapack 电网级储能系统，同时还正在得州休斯敦附近建设一座年产能达 100GW 的太阳能电池板工厂，而这座工厂与 Lumen Farm 项目位于同一个州。 然而，为了实现其得州业务的绿色供电，特斯拉却选择购买其他公司太阳能电站的电力。 这也反映出特斯拉近年来持续削减太阳能业务所留下的影响。公司当年斥资 26 亿美元收购 SolarCity 后，太阳能业务规模却大幅萎缩。年部署规模从 SolarCity 高峰时期约 870MW，降至不足当年的一小部分。特斯拉关闭了多个销售渠道，让这项业务逐渐边缘化，多年来将资源主要投入电动汽车和 Megapack 储能业务。 直到最近，特斯拉才开始重建太阳能业务。公司于 2025 年底重新推出太阳能租赁服务，今年 1 月发布了美国本土制造的太阳能板，目前又正在建设休斯敦大型太阳能板工厂。 不过，重建业务需要时间，而特斯拉显然已经等不及自家公用事业级太阳能项目建成，因此只能先通过购电协议获得所需的清洁电力。

title: AMD 与 Core Scientific 达成合作，锁定最高 2.5GW AI 数据中心算力资源
content: IT之家 7 月 28 日消息，AMD 当地时间周二宣布与 Core Scientific 达成合作协议，将获得最高 2.5 吉瓦的数据中心容量，以满足人工智能计算需求持续增长背景下对基础设施的扩张需求。 受消息影响，Core Scientific 盘前股价上涨 6%，而 AMD 股价则下跌 4%，走势与其他芯片厂商基本一致。 随着云服务提供商和企业不断加大 AI 基础设施投资，电力、土地以及数据中心资源的需求持续攀升。 据IT之家了解，根据协议，在满足特定商业条件的情况下，AMD 将获得按市场价格购买 Core Scientific 普通股的认股权证。双方并未披露交易的具体财务条款。 此次合作将使 AMD 自 2027 年起获得 Core Scientific 超过 500 兆瓦的 AI 数据中心容量，其客户可利用这些设施部署人工智能系统。未来，这一容量还可进一步扩展至最高 2.5 吉瓦。 近年来，Core Scientific 正逐步从加密货币业务转向承接 AI 和高性能计算（HPC）工作负载托管。根据协议，该公司还将与 AMD 合作开展数据中心物理基础设施设计，并部署 AMD 的芯片和软件解决方案。 AMD 企业发展战略负责人 Mathew Hein 表示：“Core Scientific 丰富的 AI 数据中心资源，将进一步扩大客户获取 AI 基础设施的渠道，帮助他们大规模部署基于 AMD 的人工智能解决方案。”

title: AMD 正式推出 Radeon RX 9050 显卡，26.7.1 驱动同步发布
content: IT之家 7 月 28 日消息，AMD 现已在官网正式列出 Radeon RX 9050 显卡，AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition 26.7.1 显卡驱动应用程序也同步上线。 Radeon RX 9050 主要面向 1080p“中等”设置游戏需求。其 拥有 16 个计算单元 (CU) ，对应 1024 个流处理器，GPU 提升频率最高可达 2600MHz、游戏频率 1920MHz，峰值 FP16 矢量性能 10.6 TFLOPs。 该显卡配备 32MB Infinity Cache， 最大显存容量 8GB ，对应 128-bit 显存接口，搭配最高可达 18Gbps 等效速率的 GDDR6 显存（IT之家注： 还提供 64-bit 4GB 版本 ）。 其支持 DisplayPort 2.1a、HDMI 2.1b 规范；保留了完整的编解码支持； 典型板载功耗（台式机）92W ；额外电源连接器 1x8-Pin，推荐基本电源 450W。 AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition 26.7.1 显卡驱动应用程序在支持这款新显卡的同时还 提供了对《战争机器：事变日》测试版与《失控进化》的支持 ，并修复了以下问题： 在 Radeon RX 7000 系列及以上显卡上运行 Maxon Cinema 4D 和 Blender 时，可能会出现模型闪烁或渲染失败的情况。 在 Radeon RX 7000 系列及以上显卡上运行 Blender 时，处理某些模型可能会导致应用程序间歇性崩溃。 在 Radeon RX 7000 系列及以上显卡上玩《堡垒之夜》时，方向指示图标可能无法渲染。 在 Windows 10 系统上，若启用 AMD FSR 超分辨率 4.1 功能，Radeon RX 7000 系列及以上显卡在运行某些游戏时可能会出现间歇性应用程序崩溃。 在 Radeon RX 9000 系列及以上显卡上启用了 AMD FSR 超分辨率和 AMD FSR 帧生成功能后，在《战地风云 6》游戏期间，这些功能在 AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition 中可能会显示为未激活状态。

title: ScaleFlux 发布 PCIe Gen6 NVMe SSD 控制器与 CXL 3.2 Type 3 内存控制器
content: IT之家 7 月 28 日消息，存储和内存解决方案企业 ScaleFlux 美国加州当地时间今日发布了其 PCIe 6.0 NVMe 固态硬盘控制器（主控）FC6116 和 PCIe Gen6 / CXL 3.2 Type 3 内存控制器 MC600，进一步扩展了其高性能产品组合。 FC6116 支持 1×4 与 2×2 两种端口配置，顺序读取速率至高可达 28GB/s、顺序写入速率至高可达 25GB/s、4KB 随机读取至高可达 7000K IOPS，稳态 4KB 随机写入超 1000K IOPS，活动功率＜9W。 其适配 SLC / TLC / QLC NAND 闪存，容量可达 256TB，支持 EDSFF E1.S/ E1.L/ E3.S/ E3.L 和 U.2 / U.3 外形规格。 FC6116 专为大规模 AI 存储部署而设计， 提供完整的 PCIe Gen6 ×4 带宽和优秀的能效 ，带来更高的存储密度和更低的 TCO。 另一方面， MC600 这款 CXL Type 3 内存控制器基于 PCIe Gen6 PHY（物理层）并符合 CXL 3.2 规范，在 PCIe Gen6 x8 配置下典型功耗低于 9W。 其支持 2DPC 四通道（每通道 40-bit）DDR5、2DPC 双通道（每通道 72-bit）DDR4，兼容 RDIMM 与 UDIMM 内存模组， 配合 DDR5 能实现至高 2TB 的容量 ，支持 PCIe AIC、EDSFF E3.S 等外形规格，计划 2026Q4 出样。 相关阅读： 《 ScaleFlux 推出服务器启动盘优化 PCIe 5.0 主控，支持 DRAM-less \ DRAM 方案 》(2024/10/10)

title: Unity 中国 CEO 张俊波：世界模型来了，但“一句话生成游戏”还不现实
content: IT之家 7 月 28 日消息，据第一财经今天报道，Unity 中国 CEO 张俊波在团结引擎 2.0 发布会后表示，他部分认同 AI 会颠覆软件、大规模提高生产效率， 但并不认为 AI 会颠覆游戏引擎 。 他对此表示：“AI 对引擎公司来说反而是好事”。AI 能降低游戏开发和使用引擎的门槛，也意味着引擎公司可以在游戏行业里渗透得更深入。 从长远看，世界模型确实能快速生成虚拟空间，但能够观看和体验的世界，并不等同于一款可以长期运营的游戏。无论是 AI 3D 生成模型还是未来的世界模型， 都更像是资产。 而游戏是一项系统工程，不仅需要画面和场景，还需要玩法规则、数值系统、交互逻辑，并能够持续迭代和长期运营。 张俊波还对行业的某些想法泼了一盆冷水：“我不大相信‘一句话生成游戏’这种话。写对联都不止一句话，能做出啥？” 据IT之家早些时候报道 ，Unity 中国今日发布团结引擎 2.0，全面贯通全球主流终端并将 AI 深度融入生产流程。 团结引擎 2.0 对引擎底层架构进行了全面重构，围绕核心引擎能力、跨平台部署、AI 原生架构三大方向完成升级，推出可独立执行游戏开发任务的 AI  Agent 团结 Codely，并打通从研发、测试到营销、发行的完整链路。 跨平台方面，团结引擎 2.0 正式新增对 PlayStation 5、XBOX Series X|S、Nintendo Switch 2 和 Nintendo Switch 主机平台的开发支持，进一步完善跨平台开发能力，形成覆盖 PC、移动端、主机、微信及抖音小游戏、开源鸿蒙、智能汽车座舱的完整矩阵，同时贯通全球主流终端与中国本土数字生态。

title: be quiet! 德商德静界推出 Light Loop IO LCD 系列水冷，自带 2.1 寸圆形屏幕
content: IT之家 7 月 28 日消息，be quiet! 德商德静界今天宣布推出 Light Loop IO LCD 系列一体式水冷散热器，新品提供黑白两种配色，带有 2.1 英寸圆形屏幕，定价 224.90 美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1524 元人民币）起。 据介绍，这款水冷可选 240mm/360mm 两种冷排尺寸， 冷头上带有一块 2.1 英寸的 IPS 面板 ， 分辨率为 480*480 ，最高亮度 500nits，可显示硬件信息、视频和图片。 规格方面，这款水冷带有高密度鳍片结构，可提升散热效率，应对旗舰级 CPU 散热需求。配备渐进式 IC 控制技术，可让水泵实现低噪音运行。其串联式 Light Wings LX PWM 高速风扇采用漏斗形出风口设计和全新扇叶结构，可带来更好的散热效果。 此外，这款产品将随机附赠 IO Controller 控制器，只需一根线缆就能传输屏幕信号和供电。配套软件 IO Center 支持自定义 ARGB 灯效、风扇转速等。

title: 《赛博朋克：边缘行者》衍生 2.5D 格斗游戏曝光，WayForward 工作室开发
content: IT之家 7 月 28 日消息，据游戏媒体 IGN 今天报道，《赛博朋克：边缘行者》2.5D 横板格斗游戏最近曝光，不过该游戏的开发状态目前无法确认。 据报道，该项目由 WayForward 工作室开发，代号“Gemini”， 自 2025 年开始便进入制作阶段 。 玩法方面，这款游戏在规划阶段拥有“回滚机制”（rollback-driven），画风偏向动画，类似《热血硬派国夫君外传热血少女》系列游戏。 值得注意的是，WayForward 去年曾因资金问题取消一款未官宣的外部 IP 游戏，并导致工作室于去年 9 月裁员，但我们目前无法确认这个被砍项目是否是“Gemini”。 截至IT之家发稿，CD Projekt 暂未回应置评请求。

title: 东风日产启辰 × 哈啰首台 Robotaxi 交付：CLTC 续航 510 公里，拥有 3.64 立方米乘员舱
content: IT之家 7 月 28 日消息，东风汽车今日宣布，旗下东风日产启辰联合哈啰开发的 首款量产自动驾驶车型 HR1 近日在广州花都工厂正式交付。 据介绍，HR1 从签约到首车落地不到一年， 以东风日产启辰 VX6 纯电 SUV 为基底开展车规级正向研发 ，整车架构设计阶段就将自动驾驶软硬件深度融合，并适配了商业化运营标准。 针对共享出行高强度使用场景，研发团队采集全国多城真实路况数据，复现各类道路行驶工况， 完成数十万公里车体台架耐久验证 。 该车空间得房率 90%， 拥有 3.64 立方米乘员舱 ；搭载的电池通过 146 项测试，满足 2026 电池新国标；采用笼式车身 + 超高强钢材设计； CLTC 续航 510 公里 ，3C 超充 30%-80% 仅 14 分钟，兼容绝大多数公共充电桩。 IT之家从东风汽车了解到， 首批 HR1 将率先在广州、深圳开启常态化运营 ，并于 1 年内陆续覆盖至少 10 座城市。

title: 前沿 AI 模型限制令生效之际，OpenAI 奥尔特曼本周将赴华盛顿
content: IT之家 7 月 28 日消息，据《政治报》昨天报道，OpenAI 首席执行官萨姆 · 奥尔特曼（Sam Altman）预计将于周三前往华盛顿，与白宫官员和国会两党议员举行会谈，讨论美国的人工智能政策。 据消息人士透露，奥尔特曼此行预计将与美国财政部长斯科特 · 贝森特（Scott Bessent）、美国商务部长霍华德 · 卢特尼克（Howard Lutnick）以及参议院网络安全核心小组联合主席马克 · 华纳（Mark Warner）。 OpenAI 上周表示，奥尔特曼此行将在宾夕法尼亚大道两端（指白宫和国会）展示最新 AI 模型。 值得注意的是， 奥尔特曼这次很可能要回应 OpenAI 最新模型如何自主实施网络攻击 。据悉，此前从未有 AI 在没有人类指挥的情况下，自行实施网络攻击。 同时，奥尔特曼还将讨论白宫 6 月行政令的落实情况。 美国政府 6 月发布的行政令将于 8 月 1 日生效， 该行政令要求各大公司发布前沿 AI 模型 30 天前 ， 自愿将其提交给政府进行安全测试 。模型发布后应向政府批准的合作伙伴进行有限部署，完成初步测试后才能向公众开放。 据三位知情人士透露，这一行政令引发各大 AI 公司的新一轮游说行动。美国政府解除 Anthropic 出口管制令后，各大 AI 公司恢复了与白宫的对话。 其中一位接近政府人士透露，OpenAI、Anthropic 和谷歌上周罕见地“团结一心”，向白宫国家网络主任办公室提交一份草案， 要求修改政策红线 。 OpenAI、Anthropic 和谷歌拒绝就此置评。

title: 华为 HiCar 迎 7.0 正式版更新，手机端可直接启动驾驶模式
content: IT之家 7 月 28 日消息，华为 HiCar 昨日在华为应用市场（App Gallery）推出 7.0.0.300 (70000300) 正式版本升级。根据要求，应用需要手机系统为 HarmonyOS 6.0 及以上版本，并在支持 HUAWEI HiCar 的汽车上使用。 IT之家附华为 HiCar 本次升级内容如下： 【新增】 1、手机支持驾驶模式，可通过“设置 - 多设备协同 - HUAWEI HiCar -驾驶模式”打开 2、智慧桌面新增桌面布局（仅部分车机支持） 3、更多应用支持摇一摇导航流转 【优化】 1、优化部分场景下的连接稳定性 IT之家实测，在升级最新版的 HiCar 后，用户可以在手机端直接启动驾驶模式，该模式可以简单理解为 HiCar 手机版， 其布局页面也与车机端的 HiCar 类似 。该模式此前已在鸿蒙 4.X 版本系统推出过，不过当时仅支持竖屏使用。而值得一提的是，最新版的驾驶模式已支持横屏使用，体验会更加友好。 据介绍，HiCar 智行是华为推出的手机和汽车互联产品，通过简单的连接，用户即可在驾驶时通过车机来使用手机的导航、音乐、电话、语音交互等功能。今年 5 月，华为 HiCar 官宣已与 70 多个汽车品牌建立合作关系，累计装车量超过 4000 万，合作车型超过 600 款。

title: 奥地利拟限制 14 岁以下儿童使用社交媒体，草案进入评估阶段
content: IT之家 7 月 28 日消息，奥地利联邦政府限制 14 岁以下儿童使用社交媒体法律草案已于昨日进入评估阶段，并传讯至欧盟委员会。 该草案将影响 TikTok、Instagram、YouTube 和 Snapchat 等社交媒体平台 ，WhatsApp 等即时通讯服务则不受影响。 根据草案规定，未来用户注册上述社交媒体时， 平台方必须对用户年龄进行验证 ，存量用户需在后续完成年龄验证。不过该法案并未规定具体验证方式，仅要求平台必须采用符合技术标准、注重隐私的方式完成验证。 同时，该法案并未完全禁止 14 岁以下儿童使用社交媒体， 平台方可选择为儿童提供不具备“上瘾风险”的专属互动区域 。但如果平台方未履行法规将面临处罚，大型平台最高可被罚款全球年度营业额的 6%。 此外，该法案将“上瘾风险”定义为具有推荐算法、无限滚动机制、自动播放功能、鼓励持续使用等。奥地利政府认为，上述机制会让儿童依赖社交媒体，因此需要出手限制。

title: 富士 instax mini 99 拍立得相机“经典银”配色明日上市
content: IT之家 7 月 28 日消息，富士官方今天宣布，instax mini 99 拍立得相机“经典银”配色将于明日 20:00 上市。新品主打复古美学基因，用银色营造出机身的立体层次。 据IT之家了解，富士 instax mini 99 拍立得相机最初于 2024 年 3 月发布，当时推出了黑色皮质纹理机身，海外版单机售价为 199.95 美元； 国行版单机 1599 元 ，曾推出包含相机包、日期章等配件的“灼灼流光”礼盒，售价 1899 元。 作为一款定位高端的拍立得相机，instax mini 99 的核心特点包括支持摄影师控制色彩、亮度和焦距，配备了色彩效果拨盘（提供绿调、暖调、蓝调等 6 种效果）、曝光补偿转盘、晕影模式物理开关以及多种拍摄模式（双重曝光、B 门模式等）。

title: 极狐阿尔法 T7 新车「幻影绿」亮相，华为乾崑 × 宁德时代 × 麦格纳三重加持

title: 消息称苹果智能家居中枢将搭载全新 Siri AI，将于今秋至明年初发布
content: IT之家 7 月 28 日消息，据彭博社的马克 · 古尔曼报道，知情人士透露，苹果计划很快推出一款以全新 Siri AI 助手为核心的智能家居中枢设备。 知情人士还表示，苹果同时准备推出一款新的 Apple TV 和升级版 HomePod mini。这两款产品在外观上“与现有版本基本保持一致”，但内部将搭载性能更强的芯片，以支持 Siri AI 功能。 据报道，苹果备受期待的智能家居中枢设备目前有两个版本正在开发。其中一个采用半球形底座设计，屏幕安装在底座顶部；另一个则通过全新的磁吸系统固定在墙面上。报道称，这款设备将配备一块 7 英寸方形显示屏，并围绕 Siri AI 打造。其将运行一套基于 tvOS 全新开发的操作系统，界面融合了 tvOS 和 watchOS 的设计风格，支持应用程序、图标以及小组件。 此外，这款设备还将支持 FaceTime 视频通话、家庭安防监控、HomeKit 智能家居生态，并提供类似 Apple Watch 的可自定义表盘功能。 其中最引人注目的新功能预计将是面部识别。报道称，该设备能够识别正在查看屏幕的用户身份，判断用户与屏幕之间的距离，并实时调整界面显示内容。系统会根据观看者自动调整信息的大小和展示方式，以获得更好的浏览体验，同时还能根据当前用户显示其个人日历、备忘录等个性化内容。 最后，报道还透露，苹果还有另外两款智能家居产品正在研发，发布时间会更晚。其中包括一款配备 9 英寸显示屏、定位更高端的机器人版家庭中枢，以及一款功能更先进的家用安防摄像头。 报道称，苹果计划于今年秋季推出新款 Apple TV 和 HomePod mini，而智能家居中枢设备则将于 10 月至明年年初期间发布。 IT之家注意到，这一举措将使苹果与亚马逊公司和谷歌在人工智能技术不断进步的市场中展开更直接的竞争。苹果的新款智能设备将与亚马逊的 EchoShow 以及谷歌的 NestHub 展开较量。

title: 遏制黄牛炒卡：日本宝可梦官方卡牌店引入人脸识别系统
content: IT之家 7 月 28 日消息，由于黄牛炒货问题愈发严重，日本五家宝可梦官方卡牌商店已开始引入人脸识别系统。 宝可梦公司于 7 月 24 日在官网宣布，位于宫城、东京、爱知、广岛和福冈的五家官方卡牌门店已引入这套系统，所有进店的成年顾客和小学以上儿童都需要进行人脸识别。 官方表示，此举旨在为所有顾客提供安全、安心的购物环境， 上述店铺每人每天只能入店一次 。如果人脸识别系统检测到有人尝试一天内多次进入商店，将在屏幕上显示相应通知。 IT之家了解到， 所有顾客进店前都需要同意人脸识别规则 ， 并领取入店号牌 。如果购物时需要去洗手间或临时离开，则需要通知店员。 虽然官方的措辞非常委婉，但结合近期宝可梦卡牌二手倒卖现象，这种政策显然是为了打击黄牛，还普通玩家一个正常的购物环境。

title: Hightech-Preise Bayern: Schweinfurter THWS-Absolvent wird von Wissenschaftsminister Blume ausgezeichnet
content:
Hightech-Preise Bayern: Schweinfurter THWS-Absolvent wird von Wissenschaftsminister Blume ausgezeichnet

Bayerns Wissenschaftsminister Markus Blume (li.) überreichte einen von fünf Hightech-Absolventenpreisen an THWS-Absolvent Shubham Joshi
StMWK/Andreas Gebert
| Copyright:
StMWK/Andreas Gebert
Mehrfach prämierte Robotik-Bachelorarbeit von Shubham Joshi erhält Absolventenpreis sowie Preisgeld von 2.000 Euro
Über die Auszeichnung mit dem Hightech-Preis Bayern in der Kategorie Absolventenpreis darf sich Shubham Joshi, Absolvent der Technischen Hochschule Würzburg-Schweinfurt (THWS), freuen. In einer feierlichen Zeremonie in München überreichte der Bayerische Staatsminister für Wissenschaft und Kunst, Markus Blume, dem ehemaligen Schweinfurter Robotik-Studenten seine Urkunde, womit auch ein Preisgeld von 2.000 Euro verbunden ist.
Der Preis wird an Absolventinnen und Absolventen der Ingenieurwissenschaften an bayerischen Hochschulen und Universitäten verliehen und zeichnet hervorragende Hochschulabschlüsse oder Promotionen aus. In der Absolventen-Kategorie wurden insgesamt fünf junge Ingenieurinnen und Ingenieure ausgezeichnet. Wissenschaftsminister Markus Blume in seiner Festansprache: „Herzlichen Glückwunsch an unsere Preisträgerinnen und Preisträger: Sie beweisen einmal mehr: Bayerns Hochschulen sind Innovationsschmieden und Problemlöser.“
Shubham Joshi wird für seine Arbeit zur Optimierung der Bestimmung der Greifposition für Pakete in der Logistik ausgezeichnet. Für seine Bachelorarbeit war er bereits von der Hans-Wilhelm Renkhoff Stiftung prämiert worden, außerdem hatte er dafür auch den „VDE Bayern Award“ erhalten. Für die Prämierungen war er jeweils von seinem Betreuer, Prof. Dr. Volker Willert, vorgeschlagen worden. „Wir arbeiten auch momentan noch zusammen, um weitere Veröffentlichungen fertig zu machen“, so Prof. Dr. Willert. Die aktuellen Robotik-Bachelorstudierenden führten zudem die Arbeit von Shubham Joshi am Center für Robotik der THWS in Schweinfurt fort – „und er ist weiterhin in Kontakt, beispielsweise um ihnen die Software zu erklären“.
Leben von Menschen mit Behinderung verbessern
Momentan absolviert Shubham Joshi ein Robotik-Masterstudium an der Technischen Universität München und arbeitet parallel am Deutschen Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt (DLR). Was ihn antreibt: Er trägt selbst Cochlear-Implantate und möchte mit seiner Arbeit das tägliche Leben von Menschen mit Behinderung erleichtern. Am DLR arbeitet er daran, einen Rollstuhl mit einem robotischen Arm auszustatten, der es Menschen ermöglicht, selbstständig zu essen oder andere Alltagstätigkeiten auszuführen.
Über Shubham Joshis Abschlussarbeit
Die Abschlussarbeit entwickelt das Fachgebiet Computer Vision weiter, also computerbasiertes Sehen, ein Teilbereich der künstlichen Intelligenz. In seiner Bachelorarbeit „Leveraging Geometric Constraints in 6D Grasp Pose Estimation of Top-Face of Rectangular Cuboids from RGB-D Data" erarbeitete der THWS-Absolvent einen neuen Ansatz, um die 6D-Pose (die Lage und Orientierung im Raum) von rechteckigen Flächen schnell und hochgenau aus einem Kamerabild inklusive einer Tiefenkamera zu errechnen. Damit lässt sich zum Beispiel die Raumlage von Kartons bestimmen, auch wenn sie nur teilweise zu sehen sind, außerdem lässt sich die passende Greifpose errechnen. Dies ist wichtig, damit ein autonomer Roboter zuverlässig und sicher Kartons in einem Warenlager greifen und verladen kann. Damit treibt die Abschlussarbeit die Automatisierung in der Logistik voran und entlastet Menschen von schwerer Arbeit.
Über die Hightech-Preise Bayern
Neben den fünf Absolventenpreisen wurde außerdem der Nachwuchspreis mit einer Dotierung von 30.000 Euro an Dr. Lukas Burgholzer von der Technischen Universität München verliehen. Der Hauptpreis – der Hightech-Preis des Bayerischen Ministerpräsidenten – ist mit 300.000 Euro die höchstdotierte Auszeichnung für Technik- und Ingenieurwissenschaften in Deutschland. Ihn erhielt Prof. Dr. Daniela Rus vom US-amerikanischen Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT). Sie ist Expertin für Robotik und Autonome Systemtechnik. Damit zeichnete die Bayerische Staatsregierung zum zweiten Mal gemeinsam mit der Bayerischen Akademie der Wissenschaften (BAdW) wegweisende Forschung und Innovationen aus.

title: Leistungsschub mit KI – Quantencomputing-basierte Methoden machen das Training großer KI-Modelle effizient
content:
Leistungsschub mit KI – Quantencomputing-basierte Methoden machen das Training großer KI-Modelle effizient

Das Bildmaterial darf nur in Zusammenhang mit dem Inhalt dieser Pressemitteilung verwendet werden. Die Quanten-Computing-Spezialisten des Fraunhofer IIS, der infoteam Software AG und OptWare GmbH im Projektteam QC-Train.
Christina Müller
| Copyright:
Fraunhofer IIS / Christina Müller
Erlangen/Nürnberg: Das Training moderner KI-Modelle erfordert enorme Rechenressourcen, verbunden mit hohem Energieverbrauch und erheblichen CO₂-Emissionen. Das QC-Train Projektteam aus der infoteam Software AG, dem Fraunhofer-Institut für Integrierte Schaltungen IIS, der OptWare GmbH sowie den assoziierten Partnern DATEV und Schaeffler Technologies arbeitet an einer quantencomputing-basierten Lösung, um hier deutliche Einsparungen am Emissionsverbrauch bei gleichzeitigem Ausbau der Leistungsfähigkeit für das Training großer Basismodelle zu erreichen. Das Projekt wird im Rahmen der Verbundforschungsprogramm »Digitalisierung« (BayVFP) des Freistaates Bayern gefördert.
Die zunehmende Verbreitung großer KI-Sprachmodelle (Large Language Models, LLMs) wie ChatGPT, Gemini uvm. sowie spezialisierter Surrogat-Netzwerke, die komplexe physikalische, technische oder mathematische Systeme datenbasiert approximieren, führt zu einem steigenden Hunger nach Rechenleistung, Energie und Speicherressourcen. Das Training dieser Modelle bringt Rechenzentren an technische und wirtschaftliche Grenzen. Vor diesem Hintergrund fordert auch der EU AI Act mehr Transparenz hinsichtlich des Energieverbrauchs von KI-Systemen und unterstützt die Entwicklung von Standards zur Steigerung der Ressourcen- und Energieeffizienz.
Mit KI und Quantencomputing gegen den KI-Datenhunger
Wie lässt sich dieser stetig steigende Bedarf an Rechenpower, der sich mit jedem Prompt und jedem zusätzlichen Training weiter erhöht, in den Griff bekommen? Herkömmliche Ansätze reichen dazu längst nicht aus. Die Quantenexpertinnen und -experten des Fraunhofer IIS entwickeln daher zusammen mit ihren Partnern eine Lösung, die die Brücke zwischen den noch nicht-gehobenen Potenzialen von Quantencomputing mit denen spezialisierter KI-Algorithmik schlägt. Im Projekt QC-Train sollen daher Trainingsmethoden dieser großen KI-Modelle komplett neu gedacht und aufgebaut werden. »Dabei sollen die ressourcenintensivsten mathematischen Operationen von derzeit noch verwendeter traditioneller Hardware auf Quantenprozessoren verlagert werden«, erläutert Dr. Daniel Scherer, Leiter der Forschungsgruppe »Quantum Compilation« am Fraunhofer IIS den grundlegenden Lösungsansatz. »Erste technische Prognosen zeigen, dass quantenbeschleunigte Trainings-Workflows eine drastische Verringerung des Ressourcenverbrauchs ermöglichen könnten und damit den Weg für eine KI der Zukunft ebnen.«
Wenige Qubits sind kein Dealbreaker
Im Projekt werden zunächst verschiedenste Strategien zur Umsetzung von Trainingsverfahren analysiert und für eine Berechnung auf Quantencomputern gestaltet. Zudem werden diese Quantensysteme auf ihre Robustheit, Skalierbarkeit und Leistungsfähigkeit getestet. Die so entwickelten Software-Werkzeuge dienen dann dazu, genau diejenigen Szenarien zu identifizieren, in denen eine Beschleunigung durch Quantenberechnung trotzdem einen deutlichen wirtschaftlichen und im Hinblick auf die Ressourceneffizienz auch ökologischen Vorteil bieten – selbst, wenn diese Quantencomputer heute noch auf wenige QuBits beschränkt sind.
Im Benchmark Leistungsfähigkeit und Ressourceneffizienz beweisen
Zusammen mit den assoziierten Partnern werden Lernmodelle auf der Basis ihrer Trainingsdaten entwickelt und bewertet, die dann in die Weiterentwicklung der Software-Werkzeuge einfließen. Zusammen mit infoteam und OptWare unterziehen die Quantencomputing-Experten des Fraunhofer IIS dann die Modelllösungen einer an der Praxis ausgerichteten Evaluierungs- und Bewertungsphase. Ziel ist es zu zeigen, dass quantenunterstützte Trainingsansätze trotz der erwarteten weiter steigenden Nutzung von KI und des damit verbundenen Rechenbedarfs einen wesentlichen Beitrag zu einer klimafreundlichen Entwicklung von KI leisten können.
Das Projekt wurde im Juli im Verbundforschungsprogramm "Digitalisierung" (BayVFP) des Freistaates Bayern gestartet und ist auf 3 Jahre angelegt.

Pakete aufs Wasser statt auf die Straße: Im Projekt A-SWARM II entwickelt die TU Berlin gemeinsam mit Partnern ein System aus elektrischen, koppelbaren Wasserfahrzeugen, das Berlins Wasserwege stärker für den Gütertransport nutzbar machen soll. Angesiedelt ist das Projekt am Fachgebiet Entwurf und Betrieb Maritimer Systeme von Prof. Dr.-Ing. Gerd Holbach. Dort wird untersucht, wie autonome Wasserfahrzeuge so gestaltet und betrieben werden können, dass sie nicht nur technisch funktionieren, sondern auch in reale Logistikketten passen.
Berlins Straßen sind voll, der Lieferverkehr nimmt zu, und freie Flächen für neue Logistikinfrastruktur sind knapp. Gleichzeitig durchziehen Wasserstraßen die Stadt – ein Verkehrsraum, der früher selbstverständlich für den Transport von Baustoffen, Lebensmitteln, Kohle, Schrott oder Müll genutzt wurde, heute aber im innerstädtischen Güterverkehr nur noch eine Nebenrolle spielt. Genau hier setzt das Forschungsprojekt A-SWARM II an: Kleine, elektrisch betriebene Wasserfahrzeuge sollen künftig autonom über Flüsse und Kanäle fahren, sich zu größeren Verbänden zusammenschließen und sich je nach Ziel wieder voneinander lösen können. „Berlin ist über Jahrzehnte auf dem Wasser versorgt worden. Mit A-SWARM II erforschen wir, wie diese vorhandene Infrastruktur für eine moderne, emissionsarme Stadtlogistik wieder aktiviert werden kann“, sagt Prof. Dr.-Ing. Gerd Holbach. „Die Idee ist nicht, den gesamten Lieferverkehr aufs Wasser zu verlegen. Aber gerade für die vorletzte Meile können Wasserstraßen eine echte Entlastung sein.“
Vom Depot auf den Kahn und von dort zum Lastenrad
Im Mittelpunkt steht zunächst der Pakettransport. Die Grundidee: Pakete werden nicht einzeln auf die Schiffe geladen, sondern in Wechselcontainern, wie sie auch bei Lastenrädern eingesetzt werden können. Ein Verteilerzentrum außerhalb oder am Rand der Stadt belädt mehrere dieser Fahrradcontainer auf die Wasserfahrzeuge. Diese fahren autonom zu wassergelegenen Umschlagpunkten, wo die Container wieder an Land gebracht werden. Von dort übernehmen Fahrradkuriere oder andere elektrische Kleinfahrzeuge die Zustellung in die umliegenden Quartiere. Damit könnte ein Teil der langen Wege zwischen Paketdepot, Mikrohub und Zustellgebiet entfallen. Nach Berechnungen aus dem Projekt könnten – je nach angenommenem Einzugsbereich entlang der Wasserstraßen – große Teile der Berliner Bevölkerung über wassernahe Liefergebiete erreicht werden. Bei 5 Kilometern Radius um die Entladestelle könnten 1 bis 1,8 Millionen Einwohner erreicht werden.
Ein Schwarm, der sich koppeln und trennen kann
Das Besondere an A-SWARM II ist das modulare Prinzip. Die im Projekt entwickelten Wasserfahrzeuge können einzeln unterwegs sein oder sich zu einem größeren Verband zusammenschließen. Auf längeren Strecken spart das Energie: Eine stärkere Einheit kann den Verband schieben, während die kleineren Fahrzeuge mitgeführt werden. Kurz vor dem Zielgebiet kann sich der Verband wieder aufteilen. Ein Teil fährt etwa nach Spandau, ein anderer Richtung Innenstadt, ein weiterer nach Köpenick – und später finden die Einheiten wieder zusammen. Was einfach klingt, ist technisch anspruchsvoll. Die Fahrzeuge müssen sich präzise zueinander positionieren, autonom navigieren, Hindernisse erkennen, miteinander kommunizieren und ihre Verbindung selbstständig herstellen und lösen können. Im Projekt wird dafür unter anderem ein magnetisches Kopplungssystem erprobt. Die Einheiten müssen dabei zentimetergenau zusammenfinden. „In der klassischen Binnenschifffahrt geht jemand mit dem Tau an den Poller. Bei A-SWARM II muss dieser Vorgang automatisch funktionieren“, erklärt Holbach. „Das betrifft nicht nur das Fahren, sondern auch das Koppeln, das Entkoppeln, das Energiemanagement und den sicheren Umgang mit der Ladung.“
Autonom fahren heißt auch autonom umschlagen
Ein zweiter Schwerpunkt liegt auf dem automatisierten Umschlag. Denn ein autonomes Schiff ist nur dann sinnvoll, wenn auch das Be- und Entladen ohne aufwendige manuelle Eingriffe möglich ist. Am Fachgebiet Entwurf und Betrieb Maritimer Systeme arbeitet das Projektteam daher an Konzepten für eine containerisierte Umschlagstation. Die Technik soll in einen 20-Fuß-Container integriert werden: Sensorik, Greifsystem, gegebenenfalls Ladeinfrastruktur und eine geschützte Arbeitsumgebung.
Das hat mehrere Vorteile. Die Station kann eingehaust werden, was die Arbeitssicherheit erhöht. Sie benötigt möglichst wenig feste Infrastruktur am Ufer. Und sie lässt sich im Idealfall versetzen, wenn ein Standort nicht funktioniert oder Genehmigungen, Flächenkonkurrenzen oder Anwohnerinteressen eine andere Lösung erforderlich machen. Gerade in Berlin ist das entscheidend: Viele frühere Gewerbe- und Umschlagflächen am Wasser sind heute Wohn-, Grün- oder Freizeitflächen.
Forschung zwischen Schiffstechnik, Energie und Logistik
Die TU Berlin bringt in A-SWARM II insbesondere ihre Expertise in maritimer Systemtechnik, Ladungsintegration, Energieversorgung und Logistik ein. Untersucht wird, welche Anforderungen unterschiedliche Güter an autonome Wasserfahrzeuge stellen: Pakete, Getränke, Lebensmittel, Müll oder andere Entsorgungsgüter brauchen jeweils andere Sicherungs-, Kühl-, Hygiene- oder Beladekonzepte. Zugleich erforscht das Team, wie viel Energie die Fahrzeuge im realen Betrieb benötigen, ob dezentrale Ladepunkte in der Stadt sinnvoll sind oder ob die Akkus für einen ganzen Betriebstag ausreichen.
Hinzu kommt eine digitale Überwachungs- und Logistikplattform. Sie soll erfassen, wo sich welches Fahrzeug befindet, wie viel Energie es verbraucht, ob Wartungsbedarf besteht und welche Einheit für welchen Auftrag am sinnvollsten eingesetzt werden kann. Ziel ist ein System, das nicht nur autonom fährt, sondern Aufträge dynamisch, energieeffizient und logistisch sinnvoll verteilt.
Die Fahrzeuge werden derzeit im Berliner Westhafen erprobt. Sie sind fahrbereit und lernen Schritt für Schritt, sich autonom zu orientieren, Hindernissen auszuweichen und sich zu koppeln. Bis zum Projektende 2027 soll demonstriert werden, wie autonome Fahrt, automatisierter Umschlag und Paketlogistik zusammenwirken können.
Reallabor für die Stadt von morgen
A-SWARM II baut auf dem Vorgängerprojekt A-SWARM auf und nutzt Synergien aus DigitalSOW, einem Projekt zur Digitalisierung und Automatisierung der Spree-Oder-Wasserstraße. A-SWARM II geht einen Schritt weiter: Es soll zeigen, wie ein künftig autonomes, flexibles und elektrisch betriebenes System aussehen könnte, das sich in bestehende Stadtlogistik integrieren lässt. Partner wie DHL nutzen bereits rein elektrische solargestützte Schiffe in Berlin und sammeln praktische Erfahrungen mit Pakettransporten auf dem Wasser, die dann in das Projekt einfließen.
Damit das neue System eine Zukunft hat sind noch technische und rechtliche Fragen zu lösen. Während autonome Fahrzeuge auf der Straße inzwischen einen ersten regulatorischen Rahmen haben, steht die autonome Binnenschifffahrt in urbanen Räumen vielerorts noch am Anfang. Gerade deshalb ist A-SWARM II auch ein Signal an Politik, Verwaltung und Wirtschaft: Die Wasserstraße kann mehr sein als Kulisse, Ausflugsroute oder Freizeitfläche. Sie kann wieder Teil der städtischen Versorgung werden, so die Forschenden im Projekt.
„Wer in der Stadt wohnt, konsumiert auch – und was konsumiert wird, muss transportiert werden“, sagt Holbach. „Wenn wir die Straßen entlasten, Emissionen reduzieren und Logistikflächen effizienter nutzen wollen, müssen wir alle vorhandenen Verkehrswege neu denken. Das Wasser gehört dazu.“
Über das Projekt
A-SWARM II (
https://www.tu.berlin/go269956/
) steht für „Autonome elektrische Schifffahrt auf Wasserstraßen in Metropolregionen“. Das Verbundprojekt wird vom Bundesministerium für Wirtschaft und Energie gefördert. Projektpartner sind: Berliner Hafen und Lagerhausgesellschaft mbH, DHL, Schiffbau-Versuchsanstalt Potsdam GmbH, Universität Rostock - Lehrstuhl Regelungstechnik, VEINLAND GmbH.

title: Wie wollen wir mit KI leben?
content:
Wie wollen wir mit KI leben?
In einem neuen Buch äussern sich über 40 Stimmen aus Wissenschaft, Kunst und Medien zur künstlichen Intelligenz. Sie schaffen ein vielstimmiges Werk einer menschenzentrierten Sichtweise auf die neue Technologie.
Künstliche Intelligenz gestaltet Bildung, Gesundheitswesen, Arbeit und Kreativität neu. Die öffentliche darüber schwankt oft zwischen Hype und Angst. Ein neues Buch von Robert Riener, Professor an der ETH Zürich bringt Klarheit in dieses Wirrwarr – nicht mit Fachjargon oder der Meinung eines einzelnen Experten, sondern mit einem Chor menschlicher Stimmen.
Der auf Englisch erschienene Band zeichnet ein Bild davon, wie künstliche Intelligenz die heutige Gesellschaft verändert und prägt. Neben Erkenntnissen aus der wissenschaftlichen Literatur und dem breiteren kulturellen Kontext vereinen 14 kurze Essays und ein reichhaltiges Mosaik von Stimmen aus mehr als 40 Interviews Perspektiven zu diesem Thema aus Wissenschaft, Industrie, Journalismus, Film, Musik und den Künsten.
Anstatt KI in technischen Begriffen zu erklären, präsentiert das Buch eine menschenzentrierte Sichtweise darauf, wie Menschen aus verschiedenen Disziplinen die aktuelle Debatte erleben und diese leistungsstarke Technologie anwenden. Von Bildung und Medien bis hin zum Gesundheitswesen und den Kreativbranchen beleuchten die Autorinnen und Autoren sowohl die sich abzeichnenden Chancen als auch die Herausforderungen einer KI-gesteuerten Welt.

title: Samsung’s chip workers are jumping ship to rival SK Hynix
content: Lee, an engineer at Samsung’s semiconductor division, clocks out when his shift ends. He used to work longer hours, going the extra mile to excel at his projects. But lately, he’s been coming straight home to work on his job application for the chipmaker’s South Korean rival SK Hynix, sharing tips with his coworkers on how to draft a stellar personal statement. Even his boss encourages him to make the move. “My team lead tells us all to jump ship to SK Hynix,” says Lee. He and his coworkers are feeling demoralized by the $476,000 bonus that SK Hynix is set to pay its employees, flush with record profits from making the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips that power Nvidia’s AI accelerators. The figure dwarfs what chip workers at Samsung are set to receive and is sparking an exodus. As the AI boom heats up, the semiconductor titans are waging a fierce talent war with flashy bonuses, aggressive recruiting, and even a courtroom injunction. Who wins could tilt the race to dominate the next generation of the HBM chips at the heart of the AI boom. “Except for our two team leads, my entire team [of 30 people] just applied to SK Hynix,” Lee says, referring to a job posting the company published in July. Lee, who has worked at Samsung for three years, even applied for an entry-level position at its rival. A coworker, who has worked at Samsung for eight years, applied for the same one. They both got rejected. But they’re hopeful that they’ll get a callback for a posting seeking a more experienced engineer. All employees at Samsung and SK Hynix that MIT Technology Review spoke with asked to be identified by just their last name or a pseudonym because they feared retaliation from their employer. Samsung declined to comment, and SK Hynix did not respond to requests for comment. After prolonged negotiations with its labor union, Samsung struck a deal in May to pay out 10.5% of the semiconductor division’s operating profits to employees as bonuses annually for 10 years, mostly in company stock that vests over three years. The move came after SK Hynix agreed last year to pay out 10% of operating profits to employees, which translates to $476,000 per employee this year—mostly in cash. But at Samsung, each division’s bonus is tied to its own bottom line. Chip workers in its memory division, which is also reaping a windfall from making HBM chips, are getting paid a bonus of roughly $400,000 per employee this year. But those who, like Lee, work in Samsung’s foundry division, which manufactures logic chips that companies like Tesla and Google design and has been operating at a loss, are getting a bonus of roughly $135,000 . Employees told MIT Technology Review that Samsung said it can’t give as many bonuses to divisions that aren’t performing well. Lee, after watching the labor union wrestle with the company for months, says he has felt disappointed by what he ended up with: “Even if Samsung does well in the future, I don’t think any of it will trickle down to me.” The workers’ lagging bonuses are making SK Hynix suddenly look appealing. According to a survey by the Samsung labor union in June, 81.5% of employees in the company’s foundry division, and nearly half of employees in the semiconductor division as a whole, said they wanted to go to another company in the next two years. In April, Samsung labor union chief Choi Seung-ho said more than 200 members of the union had left for SK Hynix over the past four months. On Blind , an anonymous workplace forum, a chorus of disgruntled engineers at Samsung confess that they want to defect to SK Hynix for the bigger bonuses. For decades, SK Hynix lived in Samsung’s shadow. It was the smaller, scrappier memory maker that elite engineering students at universities looked past when applying for jobs. But in 2019, Samsung downsized its HBM team, betting the market would stay niche, while SK Hynix doubled down on the technology. Then the AI boom supercharged the demand for HBMs, which feed AI chips the enormous amounts of data they need at ultra-high speed, driving prices to unprecedented levels. SK Hynix now leads the global market for HBMs, while Samsung is playing catch-up. Both companies topped $1 trillion in market value in May, and SK Hynix briefly dethroned Samsung as South Korea’s most valuable company in June. Predicting that demand for memory chips will continue to surge , the semiconductor titans are making aggressive investments to expand their business. Last month, the companies unveiled plans to invest more than $2 trillion by 2040, including a semiconductor “mega-cluster” in Yongin, a city south of Seoul. To staff the expansion, SK Hynix added 2,152 employees in the first half of 2026 alone and aims to double its manufacturing capacity in five years. Samsung plans to hire 60,000 employees over the next five years, especially for its semiconductor division. Even so, the pipeline will fall short: South Korea’s semiconductor industry will need about 304,000 workers by 2031 and faces a shortage of roughly 54,000, according to the Korea Semiconductor Industry Association. Now the longtime rivals are showering workers with big bonuses to keep—and poach—talent. “[SK Hynix] seems to target Samsung engineers when hiring because it’s a rival,” says Baek, a manager at SK Hynix. “From what I heard internally, the big performance bonuses we got were aimed at luring away talent from our competitor.” Courts are starting to weigh in. In July, Samsung won an injunction barring two former chip workers from working at SK Hynix for 18 months, on the grounds that chips are a national core technology deserving protection. “With competition in the semiconductor industry fierce, it’s necessary to establish a fair market order,” the court ruled. The talent exodus threatens a crucial advantage that Samsung still holds in the HBM race. “Samsung is the only memory maker in the world that owns a foundry business,” says Park Jun-young, a semiconductor expert at the Industrial Anthropology Laboratory, a research institute, who worked at Samsung for a decade. With the latest generation of the technology, known as HBM4, the logic chip at the base of each memory stack must be manufactured with the kind of advanced process that only foundries run. Samsung can do this in-house, while SK Hynix outsources it to the Taiwanese foundry giant TSMC. “If Samsung keeps losing engineers in the foundry … the collaboration between memory division and foundry division could become difficult,” says Park. “SK Hynix, which used to have only a memory team and is now hiring foundry engineers, could do better research on HBMs.” Choi, an engineer who has worked at Samsung for seven years, says he was once a star on his team, getting glowing performance reviews from his managers. But lately, he and his coworkers have been busy applying for every SK Hynix job posting they see. “We tell each other when the next SK Hynix job posting is up,” he says. “There’s always more work to do beyond our basic duties. But there’s no point in doing it.”
